Thought: I need to determine which of the given methyl halides (CH3X) is the most reactive in nucleophilic substitution reactions. In nucleophilic substitution reactions, the reactivity depends on the strength of the carbon-halogen bond and the leaving group ability of the halide.

The reactivity order for alkyl halides in nucleophilic substitution reactions is:
CH3I > CH3Br > CH3Cl > CH3F

This order is based on the leaving group ability of the halide ions, which follows the trend:
I- > Br- > Cl- > F-

Iodide (I-) is the best leaving group because:
1. The C-I bond is the weakest among these halides (lowest bond dissociation energy)
2. Iodide is the most polarizable and can best stabilize the negative charge
3. Iodide is the least basic of these halides

Therefore, CH3I (methyl iodide) is the most reactive in nucleophilic substitution reactions.
Final Answer: The most reactive compound in nucleophilic substitution reactions among the given options is methyl iodide (CH3I).
